extracted.intended_audience: emergency management personnel, public information officers, healthcare emergency managers, hospital administrators, and other responders seeking FEMA independent study training
extracted.subtask_description: A listing of FEMA Independent Study (IS) courses and short descriptions/objectives (NIMS, ICS courses, Public Information, ESF #8) for personnel seeking foundational and role-specific emergency management training.

rubrics_metrics.name: FEMA Student Identification (SID) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent Study Exams now require a FEMA Student Identification (SID) Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not yet have a SID, register at: https://cdp.dhs.gov/femasid

rubrics_metrics.name: NIMS comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMS - the National Incident Management System - is an approach to guide departments and agencies at all levels of government and the private sector to work together and manage incidents involving all threats and hazards—regardless of cause, size, location, or complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent Study Course Link: http://www.training.fema.gov/is/courseoverview.aspx?code=IS-700.a; see NIMS Training Program Guidebook: http://www.fema.gov/pdf/emergency/nims/nims_training_program.pdf

rubrics_metrics.name: ICS 100 foundational understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: ICS 100 - Introduction to the Incident Command System - introduces the Incident Command System (ICS) and provides the foundation for higher level ICS training. This course describes the features, principles, and organizational structure of the Incident Command System. It also explains the relationship between ICS and the National Incident Management System (NIMS).

rubrics_metrics.name: ICS 100.HC (healthcare) understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: ICS 100.HC - Introduction to the Incident Command System for Healthcare/Hospitals - introduces the Incident Command System (ICS) and provides the foundation for higher level ICS training using healthcare/hospital examples and exercises; uses the same objectives and content as other ICS courses with healthcare examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent Study Course Link: http://www.training.fema.gov/is/courseoverview.aspx?code=IS-100.HCb; Note: IS-100.HCb is an updated version of IS-100.HC; courses are equivalent for credentialing purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICS 200 supervisory readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: ICS 200 - ICS for Single Resource and Initial Action Incidents - is designed to enable personnel to operate efficiently during an incident or event within the Incident Command System (ICS). ICS-200 provides training on and resources for personnel who are likely to assume a supervisory position within the ICS.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICS 200.HCA applying ICS in healthcare organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: ICS 200.HCA - Applying ICS to Healthcare Organizations - provides training on the Incident Command System (ICS) to healthcare professionals whose primary responsibility is emergency management, including middle management within a hospital or healthcare system (e.g., physicians, department managers, unit leaders, charge nurses, hospital administrators) who would have a leadership role during an incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: IS-29 Public Information Officer Awareness objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: IS-29: Public information Officer Awareness - covers basic information about the role of a State or local Public Information Officer. The goal of this awareness course is to provide an orientation to the public information function and the role of the Public Information Officer (PIO) in the public safety/emergency management environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include: Understanding the PIO role, using tools and resources, communicating effectively, preparing the community, and communicating in an incident. Independent Study Course Link: http://www.training.fema.gov/is/courseoverview.aspx?code=IS-29

rubrics_metrics.name: IS-808 ESF #8 learning objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: IS-808: Emergency Support Function (ESF) #8 – Public Health and Medical Services. At the end of this lesson, you will be able to: Describe the overall purpose and scope of ESF #8; Identify the supplemental assistance ESF #8 provides to State, tribal, and local governments; Identify typical actions accomplished by ESF #8 resources and teams; Describe the types of partnerships formed between ESF #8 and other response agencies and organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent Study Course Link: http://www.training.fema.gov/is/courseoverview.aspx?code=IS-808. The course situates ESF #8 within the National Response Framework and Emergency Support Functions (ESFs) operational structure.
